content:
We have carbon NMR peaks: 166.40, 131.87, 129.70 (twice), 129.01 (twice), 129.00, 52.24, 43.47, 38.60.

We need number of CH3 groups (methyl). Typically methyl carbon appears around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, but here we have peaks at 52.24, 43.47, 38.60. Those could be carbon attached to heteroatoms or carbonyl etc. 52 ppm could be O-CH3 (methoxy). 43 and 38 could be CH2 or CH3 attached to carbonyl? But we need count of CH3 groups. Could also be from aromatic? No.

We might need proton NMR to see methyl signals. Let's get proton NMR.
